questions: Did the array keep the line in view through the tightest bend, and at what signal magnitude did it saturate?
Was the 50 mm lead ahead of the axle useful or did it cause overshoot on the sharp bends?
Did the 12 mm spacing produce a smooth signal, or did readings jump when the tape edge crossed sensor boundaries?
Was the wheel track and mass sufficient for the turn rate needed, or did the robot understeer?

intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor array with 12 mm spacing and footprint, 50 mm lead ahead of the axle, and a moderate wheel track and mass. Purpose: establish a clean reference for how the array resolves the line on the oval, s-bend and slalom tracks before varying spacing, lead or span. Expected result: completion on all development tracks with low rms_error and at most a few line-loss events. If the slalom fails, I expect the span or the lead to be the cause.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Next iteration should test whether a narrower span (for example 8 mm spacing) or a shorter lead reduces oscillation, depending on the feedback from the first race.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or Integrator feedback yet. The public contract shows that the 25 mm tape is the feature to resolve and that the signal is a reading-weighted average of sensor positions, so the geometry needs to set the sensing scale well. I chose five sensors spaced 12 mm apart across x = -0.024 to +0.024 m. Their combined span of 48 mm is about twice the tape width, so the line stays inside the array through moderate offsets and the signal changes smoothly as the robot drifts. The 12 mm footprint matches the 12 mm spacing, which gives continuous coverage without large dead zones. All sensors sit at y = 0.05 m, ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it, which helps on sharp bends. The wheel track (0.12 m) and radius (0.03 m) give a moderate turning authority, and the mass (0.8 kg) with a 0.12 m by 0.16 m body keeps yaw inertia low enough for quick corrections. I expect this to complete the development tracks with few line-loss events. The main unknowns are whether the sensor span is too wide for tight slalom bends and whether the lead distance is too long for the controller to respond to.
